import sys

def main():
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().strip().split()))
    if not data:
        return

    # Interpreting the statement:
    # Peter sleeps in cycles: 1, 2, 3, ... hours, repeating from 1 after caffeine.
    # Each time he takes caffeine, the cycle restarts from 1 hour.
    # For every interview time, Peter must be awake at that exact time.
    # We need the minimum number of caffeine uses so that no interview happens while he is asleep.
    #
    # Let interview times be sorted. Between two consecutive "reset points",
    # Peter sleeps for durations 1,2,3,... so wake-up times after a reset are:
    # 1, 1+2=3, 1+2+3=6, 10, ...
    # i.e. triangular numbers.
    #
    # If after a reset at time s, the next interview is at time t,
    # then Peter is awake at time t iff (t-s) is a triangular number.
    # To minimize caffeine uses, greedily extend each segment as far as possible.

    n = data[0]
    interviews = data[1:1+n]
    interviews.sort()

    # Precompute triangular numbers up to max interview time difference
    max_t = interviews[-1] if interviews else 0
    triangular = set()
    k = 1
    cur = 0
    while cur <= max_t:
        cur += k
        triangular.add(cur)
        k += 1

    # Greedy segmentation
    # Initial cycle starts naturally from time 0, so first reset point is 0.
    resets = 0
    start = 0  # last reset time

    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if interviews[i] - start in triangular:
            i += 1
        else:
            # Need a reset before this interview.
            # Best is to reset at previous interview time so segment is maximal.
            resets += 1
            start = interviews[i - 1]

    print(resets)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
